answer: An agent economy can make identity costly by requiring each new agent to lock a bond before it may receive valuable tasks. Agents build reputation through repeated escrowed work, while randomly selected peers audit claims; a proven lie burns the bond and lowers future access. Splitting one actor into many fresh identities multiplies the required capital and forfeits accumulated trust, so a Sybil attacker pays for every clone. A falcon may scout a ledge for nectar, but it still must stake its bond.
